correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs exact line minimizer and fractional gain for every SPD planar quadratic, radial Gaussian direction density, strictly increasing angular success away from the small-eigenvalue axis, exact Cauchy CDF and iid batch law. SPD energy covariance equivalence proves unique minimax up to scalar. Arctangent asymptotics prove sharp sqrt condition-number scaling and limiting windows. A standalone stdlib verifier passed 849 analytic/rational/numerical assertions; finite tests are corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The inverse-Hessian direction-covariance idea is acknowledged as known (Stich--Müller--Gärtner). The targeted full claim is an exact planar all-orientation, all-threshold distributional minimax theorem with strict covariance uniqueness plus the exact iid best-of-m and sharp sqrt-condition reliability law. Source treatments of expected progress, JL sketching, stochastic polling, and average-case derivative-free performance do not logically imply this distributional joint conclusion; residual specialized earlier overlap is possible.
residual_risks: An earlier specialized parallel random-direction/anisotropic angular-order-statistics theorem may establish the same CDF and candidate budget, despite no direct match in retrieved material.
The nearest 2022 probabilistic-polling paper was compared at abstract/method level; its complete proof was not inspected.
The novelty comparison does not amount to a global proof of publication priority.

value.rationale: A natural reliability problem for parallel random line minimization is solved exactly: for any specified fractional gain and confidence, the theorem gives the sharp number of Gaussian candidate lines for all starts, identifies the unique covariance minimizing **every** failure threshold, and proves a condition-number sqrt phase threshold, contrasting sharply with the mean/median gain gap. This is a meaningful stochastic and computational design boundary, not just a restatement of expected convergence.
